# cdp


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Some pages need a login, a button click or a filled form before they
show useful content. A plain download cannot do these actions. This
module controls Chrome through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). CDP
is the interface used by Chrome developer tools. The module uses
[fastcdp](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcdp) for the connection.

The module uses one Chrome process for a long time. This Chrome is
separate from the Chrome that you use for browsing. The debug Chrome
listens for remote control on port 9223. It uses a separate profile. The
default profile is `~/.cache/fastcdp/cdp-chrome`. A site login in the
debug Chrome remains after a restart.

When a Chrome already listens on the port,
[`cdp_connect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_connect)
and [`cdp_ws`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_ws)
use it. The `headless` and `extra_flags` arguments then have no effect.

The functions in this module are async. Call them with `await`. In
synchronous code, wrap them in
[`syncy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#syncy), as the
examples do. Most of them are methods that this module adds to the `CDP`
connection and `Page` classes of fastcdp. These `Page` methods are the
main ones:


*Return True when the DevTools endpoint on `port` serves

``` python
# `debug_ready` checks the endpoint. An unused port returns no response.
with socket.socket() as s: s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); free = s.getsockname()[1]
assert debug_ready(free) is False
assert _debug_ready is debug_ready   # the old private name still works
# Chrome reads from `/dev/null`, not from the caller's terminal.
import tempfile
from fastcore.test import test_eq
from unittest import mock
seen = []
with mock.patch('subprocess.Popen', lambda *a, **kw: seen.append(kw)), mock.patch.dict(globals(), debug_ready=lambda port: True, _chrome_flags=lambda *a: ['chrome']):
    syncy(cdp_setup(free, user_data_dir=tempfile.mkdtemp()))
test_eq([kw.get('stdin') for kw in seen], [subprocess.DEVNULL])
```

[`CDP.eval`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp.eval)
runs a JavaScript expression in the page and returns its value as Python
data. It waits for promises to resolve. It converts objects and arrays
to dictionaries and lists. It raises
[`JSError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#jserror) when
JavaScript throws an error. `open_page` opens a new tab at a URL and
returns its `Page`.

## Managing the debug Chrome

Plain HTTP requests can inspect Chrome’s DevTools endpoint.
`/json/version` describes the browser. `/json/list` lists its open tabs.
The first cell prints both.

The second cell closes a tab, quits the browser and starts it in a
visible window with `cdp_setup(headless=False)`. Use the visible window
to log in to a site. The profile keeps the cookies after later restarts.

``` python
# List whether debug Chrome is running and which tabs it has.
import httpx
port = 9223
print('running on 9223?', _debug_running(port))
ver = httpx.get(f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/version').json()
print('browser:', ver['Browser'], '| ws:', ver['webSocketDebuggerUrl'])
for t in httpx.get(f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/list').json():
    print(' ', t['type'], '|', t['title'][:40], '|', t['url'][:50])
print('live debug ports:', [p for p in (9222, 9223, 9224) if _debug_running(p)])
```

    running on 9223? True
    browser: Chrome/150.0.7871.129 | ws: ws://127.0.0.1:9223/devtools/browser/bb4a47a3-b032-4afd-b398-83f1de66a3ab
      page | Gayathri Dhyaanam | https://vedicreader.com/
      page | New Tab | chrome://newtab/
      iframe | chrome-untrusted://new-tab-page/one-goog | chrome-untrusted://new-tab-page/one-google-bar?par
      browser_ui | Omnibox Popup | chrome://omnibox-popup.top-chrome/
      browser_ui | Omnibox Popup | chrome://omnibox-popup.top-chrome/omnibox_popup_ai
      service_worker | Service Worker chrome-extension://ilaikd | chrome-extension://ilaikdjkclophmmhodhgfmnimfeohkg
      service_worker | Service Worker chrome-extension://hbicfl | chrome-extension://hbicflpnhfmdndpibdegbnkkpngjbhf
      service_worker | Service Worker chrome-extension://epnhoe | chrome-extension://epnhoepnmfjdbjjfanpjklemanhkjgi
    live debug ports: [9223]

``` python
# Close one tab, quit the browser, and restart it in a visible window for a manual login.
import httpx, time
port = 9223
tabs = httpx.get(f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/list').json()
if tabs: httpx.get(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/close/{tabs[0]['id']}")
cdp = syncy(cdp_connect(port=port))
try: syncy(cdp.quit())                        # `quit` raises `ConnectionClosedOK` when the socket closes.
except Exception: pass
time.sleep(1.5)
assert not _debug_running(port), 'browser should be down after quit()'
syncy(cdp_setup(port, headless=False))
assert _debug_running(port)
print('headed Chrome ready on', port, '— log in, then reuse it via fetch(url, session=True)')
```

    headed Chrome ready on 9223 — log in, then reuse it via fetch(url, session=True)

### App windows

[`cdp_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_app)
opens a URL in the debug Chrome as an app window without tabs or an
address bar. Use it for a local web app. It reuses the running browser.
All windows share the same profile and logins. When no browser is
running, it starts a visible browser and waits up to `wait` seconds.

[`cdp_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_app)
returns a dictionary with these keys:

The first test checks the launch flags without starting a browser. The
second runs
[`cdp_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_app) with
Chrome stand-ins.

``` python
# Check `cdp_app` flags for a visible app window and the persistent profile. Do not launch a browser here.
flags = _chrome_flags(9223, _profile_dir(), False, ['--app=http://alpha.localhost:5001/'])
assert '--app=http://alpha.localhost:5001/' in flags
assert '--headless=new' not in flags                  # A hidden app window cannot be used here.
assert f'--user-data-dir={_profile_dir()}' in flags   # Use the same profile as `cdp_setup` so logins remain available.
assert str(_profile_dir()).endswith('cdp-chrome')
assert _profile_dir('~/x') == Path.home()/'x'         # `user_data_dir` takes priority, and `~` expands.
```

``` python
# Run `cdp_app` with a stub browser. Reuse Chrome and report its target.
# Rebind this notebook's names because `cdp_app` resolves them at call time.
# Patching `fossick.cdp` would not change the definitions in these cells.
import httpx, subprocess as _sp

_saved = (debug_ready, _sp.Popen, httpx.get)
launched = []
class _Targets:
    def json(self): return [{'id': 'target-1', 'url': 'http://alpha.localhost:5001/'}]
try:
    debug_ready = lambda port, host='127.0.0.1': True     # A debug Chrome is already running.
    _sp.Popen = lambda args, **kw: launched.append(args)
    httpx.get = lambda url, **kw: _Targets()
    r = cdp_app('http://alpha.localhost:5001/', wait=1)
finally:
    debug_ready, _sp.Popen, httpx.get = _saved

assert r['ok'] and r['reused'] is True
assert r['target'] == 'target-1'               # Find the window by its URL.
assert r['url'] == 'http://alpha.localhost:5001/' and r['port'] == 9223
assert '--app=http://alpha.localhost:5001/' in launched[0]
assert f'--user-data-dir={_profile_dir()}' in launched[0]
print('cdp_app:', {k: r[k] for k in ('reused', 'target')})
```

    cdp_app: {'reused': True, 'target': 'target-1'}

``` python
# Open two app windows on one browser and confirm the second reused the first's process.
a = cdp_app('https://example.com/')
b = cdp_app('https://example.org/')
assert a['ok'] and b['ok']
assert b['reused'], 'the second window should reuse the browser the first one started'
assert a['profile'] == b['profile']
print('windows:', a['target'], b['target'], '| reused:', a['reused'], b['reused'])
```

## Recording network requests

[`calls`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#calls) records
requests sent by a page. It always opens a new tab. With a `url`, it
loads the page and listens for `tail` seconds after the load. Without a
`url`, it listens for twice `tail` seconds.

[`calls`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#calls) returns
a dictionary keyed by request id. Each value is a request whose URL
matches `pattern`. The request id is in `rid`. When Chrome still has the
response, the value also has its body under `response_body`.
[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr)
in `fossick.core` sends a recorded request without the browser.


[`cdp_cookies`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_cookies)
exports cookies from the debug Chrome. Pass a URL or domain to get
cookies for that site. By default, it returns a list in the format
accepted by Playwright and scrapling as `cookies=`. With `as_dict=True`,
it returns `{name: value}`. `fetch(url, session=True)` calls
[`cdp_cookies`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#cdp_cookies)
and sends the cookies with the request. This sends your logged-in
session.

## Reading a live page

These methods read the page after its JavaScript runs. The page can
differ from the HTML sent by the server. `html` returns the current
HTML. `selector` returns a scrapling `Selector` for CSS and XPath
queries. `md` converts the HTML to markdown with
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md). Pass
`sel` to convert only the part that matches a CSS selector.

## Acting on a page

An agent needs to know which page elements it can click or edit. The
HTML of a full page is too long to read. `snapshot` builds a short view
from the accessibility tree. Screen readers use this tree to describe
the page. Each control becomes one line, `[#id] role "name"`, such as
`[#42] button "Add to cart"`. Chrome assigns the id to the element. With
`interactive=False`, `snapshot` also lists headings, forms and other
landmarks.

`type_text` clears a field before it types. fastcdp’s `fill_text` adds
text to the existing field value. `click_settle` clicks and waits for
the page to settle. It does not fail when a click on a single-page app
does not navigate.

`fill_form` takes a dictionary of `{label: value}`. It finds each field
by its visible label or name. It types into text fields and selects
options in drop-downs. With `submit`, it clicks the button or link with
that name. It returns a new snapshot. It raises `ValueError` when no
field matches a label or no button or link matches `submit`.

``` python
#: `click_settle` needs `expect_navigation` before the click and `click` from fastcdp 0.0.17 or later
assert all(callable(getattr(CDP, a, None)) for a in ('expect_navigation', 'click'))
```

[`ax_diff`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#ax_diff)
compares two snapshots and lists added or removed lines. It ignores
element ids because navigation changes them. It shows the action’s
changes or `(no change)`.

The next methods use CSS selectors. Use them when you know the page
markup. `node_for` returns the id of the first matching element or None.
`click_sel` clicks an element. `fill_sel` types into an element. Both
raise `ValueError` when no element matches. `eval_json` calls a
JavaScript function with Python arguments converted to JSON.

*Return the lines added or removed between two snapshots, ignoring
element ids.*

`act` runs a list of steps in order. Use it for a planned page flow.
Each step is a tuple:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Step</th>
<th>Action</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>('goto', url)</code></td>
<td>Load the URL.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>('fill', label, value)</code></td>
<td>Type the value into the field with that label.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>('click', label)</code></td>
<td>Click the button, link or element with that name.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>('select', label, value)</code></td>
<td>Choose an option in a drop-down.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>('wait', text)</code></td>
<td>Wait until the text appears.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>('wait_sel', css)</code></td>
<td>Wait until an element matches the selector.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>('read', css)</code> or <code>('read', css, label)</code></td>
<td>Read the matching part of the page as markdown.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`act` returns a dictionary with the markdown from each
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) step. The
key is the label or the selector when the step has no label. An unknown
step raises `ValueError`.

``` python
async def act(
    page:fastcdp.core.Page, steps:list
):
```

*Run a list of steps on the page and return the markdown read by each
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) step.*

## Trying it on live pages

The cells below run against debug Chrome and real sites, so the tests
skip them. They export cookies, take a form snapshot, fill a field
through a CSS selector, compare snapshots across navigation with
[`ax_diff`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cdp.html#ax_diff),
fill a form by label with `fill_form`, run the same steps through `act`,
and record a store search API with
[`calls`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#calls).

``` python
# `cdp_ws` returns the websocket URL for `scrapling`'s `cdp_url`. `cdp_cookies` exports browser cookies.
ws = cdp_ws()
assert ws.startswith('ws://'), ws
ck = cdp_cookies('https://httpbin.org', as_dict=True)
assert isinstance(ck, dict)
lst = cdp_cookies('https://httpbin.org')            # Playwright-format list for scrapling cookies=
assert isinstance(lst, list) and all(isinstance(c, dict) for c in lst)
print('ws ok |', len(ck), 'cookies')
```

    ws ok | 0 cookies

``` python
# Take a form snapshot, fill a field with a CSS selector, and compare snapshots after navigation.
cdp = syncy(cdp_connect())
pg  = syncy(cdp.open_page('https://httpbin.org/forms/post'))
snap = syncy(pg.snapshot())
assert snap.startswith('#') and '[#' in snap and 'textbox' in snap.lower()   # Snapshot lines use `[#id] role "name"`.
bid = syncy(pg.node_for('input[name=custname]'))                             # Convert a CSS selector to a `backendNodeId`.
assert isinstance(bid, int)
syncy(pg.fill_sel('input[name=custname]', 'Ada Lovelace'))                   # Clear and type through the selector.
# Navigate to another page and compare the snapshots.
syncy(pg.act([('goto', 'https://example.com')]))
diff = ax_diff(snap, syncy(pg.snapshot()))
assert diff != '(no change)'
print(diff[:200])
```

``` python
# Fill a real form by label with `fill_form`.
cdp = syncy(cdp_connect())
fp  = syncy(cdp.open_page('https://httpbin.org/forms/post'))
snap = syncy(fp.fill_form({'Customer name': 'Ada Lovelace'}))   # Return a snapshot.
assert '[#' in snap
```

``` python
# Navigate, fill a field, and read a page region as markdown.
reads = syncy(fp.act([('goto', 'https://httpbin.org/forms/post'),
                      ('fill', 'Customer name', 'Ada Lovelace'),
                      ('read', 'form', 'form')]))
assert 'form' in reads and isinstance(reads['form'], str)
```

## Screenshots and annotation

[`collect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#collect)
gathers screenshots while a person browses. It adds a bar with capture
and done buttons to the page. Each capture hides the bar before it takes
a screenshot.

[`collect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#collect)
stops when one of these events occurs:

- The person presses done.
- `count` screenshots have been taken.
- `tout` seconds have passed.
- The `stop` event is set.

With `every_n`,
[`collect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#collect) also
takes a screenshot every `every_n` seconds without a button press. With
`save_dir`,
[`collect`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#collect)
saves each screenshot there as a PNG file named from `prefix`. The
default `prefix` is the page title. It returns a list of `(image, path)`
pairs. Without `save_dir`, it returns a list of images.

`BUTTON_JS`, `HIDE` and `SHOW` draw, hide and show the bar.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cdp.py#L347"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Page.collect

``` python
async def collect(
    page:fastcdp.core.Page, save_dir:NoneType=None, prefix:NoneType=None, stop:NoneType=None, tout:NoneType=None,
    count:NoneType=None, every_n:NoneType=None
):
```

*Take screenshots from the capture button or on a timer and return
them.*

``` python
page = syncy(cdp.new_page())
syncy(page.goto('https://vedicreader.com/s/'))
imgs = syncy(page.collect(count=1, tout=5, every_n=1))
if imgs: imgs[0].width, imgs[0].height = 200, 400
imgs[0]
```

    📸 capture, ✓ done (or stop.set()) to finish. → None/

![](01_cdp_files/figure-commonmark/cell-42-output-2.png)

[`annotate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#annotate)
lets a person point to page elements. The page outlines and numbers each
clicked element. An agent can use this information to ask which button
or field the person means.

[`annotate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#annotate)
ends when the person presses done, `tout` seconds pass or the `stop`
event is set. It then takes a screenshot with the numbers. It returns
`(img, selected)`. `selected` is a list with one dictionary for each
element. Each dictionary has the keys `n`, `role`, `name` and `selector`
(a CSS selector). With `save_dir`,
[`annotate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#annotate)
also saves the screenshot as a PNG file named from `prefix`.

[`annotate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#annotate)
injects the scripts `ANNOTATE_JS`, `ANNOTATE_BAR_JS` and
`ANNOTATE_CLEANUP_JS`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cdp.py#L474"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
async def annotate(
    page:fastcdp.core.Page, save_dir:NoneType=None, prefix:NoneType=None, stop:NoneType=None, tout:NoneType=None
):
```

*Let a person click elements to number them and return a screenshot with
the numbers and a list of the chosen elements.*

``` python
img, elements = syncy(page.annotate(save_dir='shots', tout=2))
img.height, img.width = 400, 200
img
```
